{"answer":"840","trace":"Dividing 8400 by 10 moves the decimal point one place left: 8400 ÷ 10 = 840, since 840 × 10 = 8400."}

{"answer":"candela (cd)","trace":"The candela is the SI base unit of luminous intensity, defined by fixing the luminous efficacy of monochromatic 540 THz radiation at 683 lm/W. It is one of the seven SI base units."}

{"answer":"mole (mol)","trace":"The mole is the SI base unit for amount of substance, defined since the 2019 SI redefinition by fixing the Avogadro constant at 6.02214076×10^23 mol⁻¹ (one mole contains exactly that many elementary entities)."}

{"answer":"ampere (A)","trace":"The ampere is one of the seven SI base units, defined by fixing the elementary charge at 1.602176634×10^-19 C, which ties the ampere to one coulomb per second. It is the SI base unit for electric current."}

{"answer":"kelvin (K)","trace":"The kelvin is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature. Since the 2019 SI redefinition, it is defined by fixing the Boltzmann constant at exactly 1.380649×10⁻²³ J/K, so the kelvin is expressed in terms of the kilogram, metre, and second. The symbol is K."}
{"answer":"Nairobi","trace":"Nairobi has been Kenya's capital since independence in 1963, and it remains the capital today."}

{"answer":"kilogram (kg)","trace":"The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram, the base unit defined by fixing the Planck constant at 6.62607015×10^-34 J·s (2019 redefinition). It is the only SI base unit whose name contains a prefix, with the gram being the derived-form reference."}
{"answer":"second (s)","trace":"The SI base unit of time is the second, symbol s. It is defined by fixing the numerical value of the caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency at 9,192,631,770 Hz."}

answer: George Orwell (pen name of Eric Arthur Blair)
raw_text: {"answer":"George Orwell (pen name of Eric Arthur Blair)","trace":"Nineteen Eighty-Four was written by English author George Orwell and published in 1949 by Secker & Warburg. Orwell is the pen name of Eric Arthur Blair."}
{"answer":"Anemometer","trace":"An anemometer is the standard instrument for measuring wind speed; cup, vane, and hot-wire/sonic designs are common types."}

{"answer":"Hygrometer","trace":"A hygrometer is the instrument used to measure humidity (water vapor content) in air. Common types include capacitive, resistive, and dew-point hygrometers, and psychrometers (wet-bulb/dry-bulb) are also used."}

answer: Hydrometer (or a pycnometer/densitometer for precise measurements; a hydrometer floats and reads specific gravity relative to water)
raw_text: {"answer":"Hydrometer (or a pycnometer/densitometer for precise measurements; a hydrometer floats and reads specific gravity relative to water)","trace":"A hydrometer floats in a liquid and its immersion depth indicates the liquid's density or specific gravity relative to water, which has a reference value of 1.000."}

{"answer":"Ohmmeter","trace":"An ohmmeter measures electrical resistance by applying a known voltage or current to the circuit and inferring resistance from Ohm's law (R = V/I), or by using a multimeter set to its resistance (Ω) function."}

{"answer":"Voltmeter","trace":"A voltmeter is connected in parallel across the two points to measure the potential difference (voltage) between them; ideal voltmeters have very high internal resistance so they draw negligible current."}

{"answer":"Ammeter","trace":"An ammeter measures electric current and is connected in series with the circuit element whose current is being measured. Galvanometers are the underlying sensing principle; a clamp meter can measure current non-invasively."}

{"answer":"Evaporation","trace":"Evaporation is the phase change in which molecules at the surface of a liquid gain enough kinetic energy to overcome intermolecular forces and escape into the gas phase. It occurs at any temperature below the boiling point, unlike boiling, which happens throughout the liquid at a specific temperature."}

{"answer":"Sublimation","trace":"Sublimation is the phase transition in which a substance changes directly from the solid phase to the gas phase without passing through the liquid phase. The reverse process is deposition."}

{"answer":"1945","trace":"World War II ended in 1945: Germany surrendered in May 1945 (V-E Day, May 8), and Japan surrendered in August 1945 (announced August 15, formally signed September 2, 1945), which concluded the war."}

{"answer":"Condensation","trace":"Changing from a gas (vapor) to a liquid is condensation, the reverse of vaporization/evaporation. It occurs when a gas loses enough thermal energy to form a liquid, typically at or below its dew point or saturation temperature."}
{"answer":"W","trace":"Tungsten is element 74 on the periodic table; its chemical symbol W comes from its former name 'wolfram' (German)."}

{"answer":"Russia","trace":"Russia covers about 17.1 million square kilometers (roughly 17.1 million km² total area, about 16.4 million km² land area after excluding inland water), the largest of any country, followed by Canada and the United States/China."}

{"answer":"newton (N)","trace":"The SI derived unit of force is the newton, defined so that 1 N = 1 kg·m/s² (kg·m·s⁻²), i.e., the force needed to accelerate a 1 kg mass at 1 m/s², from Newton's second law F = ma."}
{"answer":"pascal (Pa)","trace":"The SI derived unit of pressure is the pascal, defined as one newton per square metre (N/m² = kg·m⁻¹·s⁻²). It is named after Blaise Pascal."}

{"answer":"joule (J)","trace":"The SI derived unit of energy is the joule, defined as 1 J = 1 N·m = 1 kg·m²/s². It is named after James Prescott Joule and is equivalent to the work done when a force of one newton acts through a distance of one metre."}
{"answer":"watt (W)","trace":"The SI derived unit of power is the watt, named after James Watt. One watt equals one joule per second (J/s), which is equivalent to kg·m²·s⁻³ in base SI units."}

{"answer":"coulomb (C)","trace":"The coulomb is the SI derived unit of electric charge, defined as the amount of charge transferred by a constant current of one ampere flowing for one second (1 C = 1 A·s). It is named after Charles-Augustin de Coulomb and is expressed in base SI units as A·s."}

{"answer":"hertz (Hz)","trace":"The SI derived unit of frequency is the hertz, defined as one cycle per second (1 Hz = 1 s⁻¹). It is named after Heinrich Hertz and is a derived unit because it is expressed in terms of the SI base unit of time, the second."}

{"answer":"ohm (Ω)","trace":"The SI derived unit of electrical resistance is the ohm, symbol Ω. It equals one volt per ampere (1 Ω = 1 V/A), or equivalently 1 kg·m²·s⁻³·A⁻² in base SI units, following from Ohm's law R = V/I."}
{"answer":"volt (V)","trace":"The SI derived unit of electric potential is the volt, defined as one joule per coulomb (1 V = 1 J/C), equivalently 1 kg·m²·s⁻³·A⁻¹."}

{"answer":"farad (F)","trace":"Capacitance is charge per unit voltage (C = Q/V). Since the coulomb (C) is the SI unit of charge and the volt (V) is the SI unit of potential difference, the SI derived unit of capacitance is the coulomb per volt, named the farad in honor of Michael Faraday. In base units it equals kg^-1·m^-2·s^4·A^2."}
{"answer":"weber (Wb)","trace":"Magnetic flux Φ = B·A; with B in tesla (T = kg·s⁻²·A⁻¹) and A in m², 1 Wb = 1 T·m² = kg·m²·s⁻²·A⁻¹ = V·s."}
{"answer":"15001","trace":"12001 + 3000 = 15001: add the thousands (12000 + 3000 = 15000), then add the remaining 1 from 12001."}
{"answer":"15007","trace":"12004 + 3003: add thousands (12000 + 3000 = 15000), then add remaining units (4 + 3 = 7), giving 15007."}
{"answer":"15035","trace":"12018 + 3017: units 8+7=15 (write 5, carry 1); tens 1+1+1=3; hundreds 0+0=0; thousands 2+3=5; ten-thousands 1. Result 15035."}
{"answer":"15037","trace":"12019 + 3018: units 9+8=17 (write 7, carry 1); tens 1+1+1=3; hundreds 0+0=0; thousands 2+3=5; ten-thousands 1. Result 15037."}
{"answer":"15045","trace":"12023 + 3022: units 3+2=5; tens 2+2=4; hundreds 0+0=0; thousands 2+3=5; ten-thousands 1+0=1. Result 15045."}
{"answer":"15047","trace":"12024 + 3023: add thousands 12000 + 3000 = 15000; add hundreds/tens/ones 24 + 23 = 47; total 15047."}
{"answer":"15057","trace":"12029 + 3028: units 9+8=17, write 7 carry 1; tens 2+2+1=5; hundreds 0+0=0; thousands 2+3=5; ten-thousands 1. Result: 15057."}

{"answer":"Tesla (T)","trace":"Magnetic flux density B is measured in teslas, where 1 T = 1 weber per square metre (1 Wb/m² = 1 V·s/m² = 1 kg·s⁻²·A⁻¹). It is the SI derived unit for B, named after Nikola Tesla."}

{"answer":"henry (H)","trace":"The SI derived unit of inductance is the henry (H), named after Joseph Henry. It is equivalent to 1 V·s/A, or equivalently 1 kg·m²·s⁻²·A⁻² (1 Wb/A). An inductance of 1 H means that a current change of 1 A per second induces an EMF of 1 V, per Faraday's law, L = Φ/I."}

{"answer":"lumen (lm)","trace":"The lumen is the SI derived unit of luminous flux, defined as the luminous flux emitted by a point source of 1 candela intensity into a solid angle of 1 steradian (1 lm = 1 cd·sr)."}
{"answer":"lux (lx)","trace":"Illuminance is luminous flux per unit area. The SI unit of luminous flux is the lumen (lm, cd·sr), so illuminance is lm/m² = cd·sr·m⁻², named the lux (1 lx = 1 lm/m²)."}

{"answer":"katal (kat), equal to mol/s","trace":"The katal is the SI derived unit of catalytic activity, defined as one mole of substrate converted per second (1 kat = 1 mol·s⁻¹). The enzyme unit (U) is a non-SI unit: 1 U = 1 µmol/min, so 1 kat = 6×10⁷ U."}
{"answer":"O3","trace":"Ozone is an allotrope of oxygen consisting of three oxygen atoms bonded together, so its molecular formula is O3 (molar mass about 48 g/mol)."}
{"answer":"CH4","trace":"Methane has one carbon atom bonded to four hydrogen atoms in a tetrahedral geometry, giving the formula CH4."}
{"answer":"NH3","trace":"Ammonia consists of one nitrogen atom bonded to three hydrogen atoms (1 N + 3 H = NH3), a trigonal pyramidal molecule."}
{"answer":"H2O2","trace":"Hydrogen peroxide has two hydrogen atoms and two oxygen atoms per molecule, bonded as H–O–O–H, giving the formula H2O2 (molar mass about 34.01 g/mol)."}
{"answer":"H2SO4","trace":"Sulfuric acid has two hydrogen atoms, one sulfur atom, and four oxygen atoms, giving H2SO4 (molar mass about 98.08 g/mol)."}
{"answer":"HNO3","trace":"Nitric acid has one hydrogen, one nitrogen, and three oxygen atoms, bonded as H-O-N(=O)-O. Molar mass is about 63.01 g/mol (H 1.008 + N 14.007 + 3 x O 15.999)."}
{"answer":"NaHCO3","trace":"Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) is one sodium ion (Na+) paired with one bicarbonate ion (HCO3-), giving NaHCO3 (molar mass about 84.01 g/mol)."}
{"answer":"CaCO3","trace":"Calcium carbonate is an ionic compound of Ca2+ and CO3 2-. Charges balance with one calcium ion per carbonate ion, giving CaCO3 (molar mass about 100.09 g/mol)."}

{"answer":"C6H12O6","trace":"Glucose is a monosaccharide (aldohexose) with six carbons, twelve hydrogens, and six oxygens. Its empirical formula is CH2O, and the molecular formula is 6 × CH2O = C6H12O6."}
{"answer":"Lima","trace":"Lima is the capital and largest city of Peru, located on the country's central coast on the Pacific Ocean. This is a well-established fact unlikely to have changed."}

{"answer":"Leonardo da Vinci","trace":"The Mona Lisa is a portrait painted by the Italian Renaissance artist Leonardo da Vinci, begun around 1503 and worked on for years afterward; it is held in the Louvre in Paris."}
{"answer":"SiO2","trace":"Silicon has valence 4 and oxygen has valence 2, so one silicon atom bonds with two oxygen atoms to balance charge, giving the empirical formula SiO2 (silica)."}
{"answer":"HCl","trace":"Hydrogen chloride consists of one hydrogen atom covalently bonded to one chlorine atom, so the empirical and molecular formula is HCl (one H, one Cl per molecule)."}
{"answer":"NaOH","trace":"Sodium hydroxide is an ionic compound of one Na⁺ cation and one OH⁻ hydroxide anion, so the empirical formula is NaOH (molar mass about 40.00 g/mol)."}
{"answer":"KNO3","trace":"Potassium (K, +1) pairs with nitrate (NO3−, −1) in a 1:1 ratio, so the neutral compound is KNO3."}
{"answer":"CaO","trace":"Calcium (Ca, valence +2) bonds with oxygen (O, valence -2) in a 1:1 ratio, so the empirical formula is CaO."}
{"answer":"MgSO4","trace":"Magnesium is Mg (+2) and sulfate is SO4 (2-). Charges balance at a 1:1 ratio, giving MgSO4 (anhydrous; the heptahydrate is MgSO4·7H2O)."}

{"answer":"Na2CO3","trace":"Sodium (Na) has a +1 charge and carbonate (CO3) has a -2 charge. Two Na+ ions balance one CO3^2- ion, giving Na2CO3 (sodium carbonate, commonly known as washing soda or soda ash)."}

{"answer":"CO","trace":"Carbon monoxide consists of one carbon atom (atomic number 6) and one oxygen atom (atomic number 8) joined by a bond, so the empirical and molecular formula is CO with a 1:1 atom ratio."}
{"answer":"H2S","trace":"Hydrogen sulfide has two hydrogen atoms bonded to one sulfur atom (H-S-H), a bent molecule with the formula H2S."}

{"answer":"SO2","trace":"Sulfur dioxide consists of one sulfur atom (S) double-bonded to two oxygen atoms (O); the subscript 2 denotes two oxygen atoms per sulfur atom, giving SO2 with molar mass about 64.07 g/mol."}

{"answer":"H3PO4","trace":"Phosphoric acid is orthophosphoric acid: phosphorus (+5) bonded to four oxygens, three of which carry ionizable hydrogens. Molar mass ≈ 98.0 g/mol (3×1.008 + 30.974 + 4×15.999)."}
{"answer":"60","trace":"One hour equals 60 minutes, since a minute is 1/60 of an hour (60 × 1 minute = 1 hour)."}
{"answer":"He","trace":"Helium is element 2 on the periodic table, a noble gas. Its standard chemical symbol is He, taken from its Latin-derived name 'helium' (from Greek helios, sun)."}
{"answer":"C6H8O7","trace":"Citric acid is a tricarboxylic acid (2-hydroxypropane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid). Its formula is C6H8O7, with molar mass about 192.12 g/mol."}
